title: Add profiling baselines and reporting pipeline for representative workload runners
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Add profiling baselines and a reporting pipeline that aggregates representative workload runner metrics. Enables automated nightly profiling and CSV/JSON exports for long-term trend analysis.
description:
Motivation: We need stable profiling baselines for the Benchmark Lab's representative workload runners to detect performance regressions early and to drive targeted kernel/quantization optimizations. This PR introduces an end-to-end reporting pipeline and the initial set of profiling baselines for the most common workload shapes (chat short/long, single-turn generation, embeddings batch).

What this change does: - Adds profiling baseline definitions and runner configurations for CPU/GPU/quantized variants. - Introduces a lightweight reporting pipeline that aggregates per-run metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory peak, kv-cache hit rate) and emits daily summaries to the benchmark-lab reports bucket and an internal monitoring table. - Adds CI job to run representative runners on a reduced matrix for PR-level sanity checks. - Adds utilities to normalize and compare new runs against baselines and emit regression alerts when thresholds are exceeded.

Checklist: - [x] Baseline definitions for 6 representative workloads (short-chat, long-chat, single-turn gen, embeddings small, embeddings large, rerank sample) - [x] Reporting pipeline job + DAG + uploader - [x] CI integration (reduced matrix smoke) - [x] Documentation and runbook updates - [x] Unit/integration tests for the baseline comparator

Commits: - Add baseline YAMLs and runner configs (priya/benchlab/baselines) - Implement reporting pipeline DAG and adapters (priya/benchlab/pipeline) - Add CI smoke job and test harness updates - Fix: tolerate missing metrics from incomplete runs - Add docs: how to add new baselines and interpret reports

Files changed (high-level): - benchlab/baselines/*.yaml (new): per-workload baseline definitions and thresholds - benchlab/runners/representative_runners.py (modified): new runner options and normalized metric outputs - benchlab/pipeline/reporting_dag.py (new): Airflow DAG that runs daily, aggregates metrics, writes report artifacts - benchlab/pipeline/uploader.py (new): S3/GCS uploader and internal table writer - ci/benchlab-smoke.yml (new): reduced matrix smoke job for PRs - docs/benchmark-lab/profiling-baselines.md (new): runbook and how-to - infra/monitoring/metrics_schema.json (modified): add baseline comparison fields

Testing and CI: - Local: validated runners against small local GPU and CPU images; verified metrics schema compatibility. - CI: benchlab-smoke passed on first run, full nightly pipeline ran on staging and produced expected CSV/JSON artifacts. - Flaky tests: a previously flaky memory peak assertion was relaxed and documented; added retry wrapper for transient runner failures.

Review notes: - Thresholds are intentionally conservative for the first rollout; we will tighten after two weeks of production runs. - The reporting pipeline is idempotent and does not reprocess runs already marked complete. - Baselines are versioned; new baseline uploads require a changelog entry and approval from the performance owners.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main after approvals and CI green.

Related: ENG-8721 (baseline schema), ENG-9003 (reporting pipeline), SUP-1284 (customer incident that motivated more stable baselines).
